army-leyte-ch8.claim: Burauen airfields: San Pablo about 5 mi west of Dulag, 2 mi east of Burauen, east-west, 164 x 4,920 ft, overgrown and unoccupied; Bayug just north of the highway, a half mile east of Burauen, about 5,000 ft; Buri about 1 mi northeast of Burauen, east-west, 5,000 ft, the most important of the three

army-leyte-ch11.claim: Mud and field construction problems; Buri and San Pablo abandoned, Bayug work continued (late Nov 1944)

army-leyte-ch17.claim: Operation Te-Go: attacks on the Buri and San Pablo airfields on 6-7 Dec 1944

marine-aviation-philippines.claim: Tacloban and Dulag construction problems; Tanauan work after 28 Nov; the inland fields abandoned

f3-j1-groups.claim: J1 tracks five critical groups at Buri: fuel farm, radio station, north hangar, south hangar, parked-aircraft dispersal

reference.source: Runway length is the Army history (ch. VIII: east-west, 5,000 ft, about 1 mi northeast of Burauen) = 1,524 m; width 45 m is an ESTIMATE carried from the other bases. Center and heading 80 are FITTED to the shipped terrain near the Army offset (tools/sites/surveyStrip.ts, 2026-10-17): all land, about 6 m of relief over 1.5 km, the best the terrain offers near that offset. Windows follow the F3 section 5 Buri row. Every building pose is invented gameplay layout; the five J1 groups (north and south hangar, fuel farm, radio station, dispersal revetments) exist because F3 section 4 J1 requires them, and are labeled inferred.

pre-invasion.note: Principal Japanese inland field; the J1 start (engine-running at Buri) and its five critical groups.
